title: CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701)

intro.about: CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701) validates the baseline skills a working security professional uses every day: assessing the security posture of an enterprise environment, recommending and implementing the right controls, monitoring and responding to incidents, and operating with an eye on governance, risk and compliance. Exam Objectives Version 5.0 defines five domains: General Security Concepts (12%), Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigations (22%), Security Architecture (18%), Security Operations (28%), and Security Program Management and Oversight (20%).
intro.audience: Aimed at early-career security practitioners — security administrators, SOC and help-desk analysts stepping up, systems and network administrators taking on security duties — CompTIA recommends a minimum of two years of IT administration experience with a security focus. Security+ is a vocabulary-dense exam: it rewards candidates who can separate near-neighbour terms (IDS from IPS, containment from eradication, controller from processor) under a described situation, not recite definitions.

materials.title: Three question formats, with performance-based questions approximated
materials.description: Single choice and select-two/select-three multiple response match the real multiple-choice mechanics. The real exam's interactive performance-based questions (PBQs) are approximated as scenario-matching and configuration-reading items — the format coverage note below carries the full disclosure.

intro.disclaimer: An independent, originally-authored study tool for personal exam preparation — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to CompTIA, Inc. or Pearson VUE. "CompTIA", "Security+" and "CompTIA Security+" are trademarks of CompTIA, Inc. Every question was written clean-room from documented derivation artefacts against the public exam objectives, with prior practice sets analyzed for classification only, exactly as this package's provenance records state. Nothing here is drawn from the live SY0-701 item bank: real exam content is confidential under the CompTIA Candidate Agreement, and CompTIA's own Authorized Materials Use Policy revokes certifications earned with brain-dump material — so never share live questions here, for your own certification's sake as much as ours.

format_coverage: The real SY0-701 exam uses a maximum of 90 questions in 90 minutes and two item classes: multiple-choice (including select-two and select-three stems) and performance-based questions (PBQs). CompTIA publishes no count or weighting for PBQs. This mock supports three formats and approximates as follows. Multiple choice with one correct response maps exactly to single_choice, four options, as in every item of CompTIA's own free practice set. Select-two and select-three multiple choice map exactly to multiple_response (five options, all-or-nothing; the stem states the count). Performance-based questions are NOT supported: a PBQ is an interactive simulation — building a firewall ruleset, dragging controls onto a topology, classifying log lines, completing a matrix — and Mockka has no simulation surface. PBQ reasoning is approximated two ways here, both of them demonstrated by CompTIA's own sample set: as scenario_matching where the task is genuinely a mapping (investigative questions onto log sources; situations onto agreement types; observed indicators onto attacks), and as scenario-led single_choice over candidate configurations where the task has one defensible outcome — CompTIA's own sampler does exactly this with an access-list item whose four options are the same rule with source/destination and permit/deny transformed. The consequence, stated plainly: the underlying judgment is rehearsed, the interaction is not. You will meet the drag-and-drop and configuration-editor interfaces for the first time in the real exam, and the real paper's PBQs typically carry more marks per item than a multiple-choice question. Note also that the vendor states 'maximum of 90' questions, so a live form may be shorter than this mock, and the real pass mark is 750 on a 100-900 scale — the 81% threshold here is a linear proxy for that scaled mark, not a vendor-published raw percentage.
